chapter: Records, Lovie Austin and a first marriage
title: Rivalry with Bessie Smith's records; not listening to others
summary: In 1923 they recorded the same numbers for different labels; Hunter says Bessie never had the chance to like her, and she did not listen to others' records but admired Bessie's voice.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: What about -- now, I notice, for instance, back in '23, which was also the year Bessie started recording, you were doing a lot of the same numbers, "'Tain't Nobody's Business, Aggravatin' Papa, "Bleeding Hearted Blues" --
Quite a big number for me, that was.
But you're doing them for Paramount, and she's doing the same songs for Columbia, you know.
They were -- must have been sort of rivalry there.
Yeah, rivalry, uh-huh. Maybe that's why she didn't like me.

I don't -- I don't think she disliked me. She didn't have a chance to like me or dislike me. But she just would -- she was just a woman just didn't bother, I guess, you know. I don't want to talk about her when she's
dead. She's not here to defend herself, you know.
But did you -- would you, for instance, at that time, when a new record came out by Bessie Smith or anyone else, would you listen to it?

No, I never listened to anybody's records. I just didn't -- it wasn't that I felt that I was better than anybody else or didn't have to listen, because you can always learn something from other people, you know. It's just that I was so wrapped up in Dreamland and, you know, just going and doing my work. I didn't listen to anybody's records.
But I used to buy them for other people.
Oh, yes. And I knew she was wonderful, and I always admired her, because I thought her -- just her voice was just so outstanding, you couldn't help but admire her.
But did you ever go, for instance, if Bessie was at the Avenue, would you go to listen to her? To catch her act or anyone else's act, for that matter?
Yes, I would. Sure, because you could learn something. I could learn something from them; however, regardless of who I heard sing, I wouldn't try to sing like them. I always had my own style.
